title: Agentforce Specialist
description: Prompt Builder, the Trust Layer, grounding with Data 360, agent topics and actions, testing and deployment. Not yet covered: Agent Script and the Spring '26 authoring model.

questions.prompt: Sales reps want a one-click, consistent summary of an account's open cases and recent activity on the account page. What fits best?

options.text: Each rep pasting the account details into a public chatbot and copying the reply
An Apex trigger that writes a summary on every account save
A report of the account's open cases and activities
A grounded prompt template in Prompt Builder

questions.explanation: Prompt Builder creates reusable, grounded templates that run from the record with consistent instructions. Public chatbots lack the org's data and the Trust Layer.

questions.prompt: Which prompt template type fills a specific field on a record page, such as a case description summary?

options.text: Flex
Record Summary
Field Generation
Sales Email template

questions.explanation: Field Generation templates are attached to a field on a Lightning record page and write their output into that field for the user to review.

questions.prompt: A template must take an Account and a Product as inputs and isn't tied to one record page. Which type fits?

options.text: Flex
Field Generation
Record Summary
Sales Email

questions.explanation: Flex templates define their own inputs, so they can combine several objects and be invoked from flows, Apex or agent actions.

questions.prompt: A template needs the case subject, the account name and the last five case comments. Which grounding techniques fit?

options.text: Merge fields, plus a related list or flow for the comments
A retriever over the whole Knowledge base, run for every request
A retriever over the whole Knowledge base for every request
Letting the model infer the details from the case number

questions.explanation: Merge fields pull values from the input record; related lists or a template-triggered flow can supply related records like comments.

questions.prompt: Grounding requires data that needs filtering and logic across several objects. What is the declarative way to provide it?

options.text: A template-triggered prompt flow
A list view filtered to the related records
A roll-up summary field that totals the related records
A validation rule that formats the related data before the prompt runs

questions.explanation: Template-triggered prompt flows run logic to gather and shape data, then pass the result into the prompt. Apex is the code-based alternative.

questions.prompt: An admin saved a new prompt template, but users can't run it. What is the likely missing step?

options.text: The template must first be approved by Salesforce
The org must be restarted after a template is saved
The template version hasn't been activated
Prompt templates only run in sandboxes until promoted

questions.explanation: Templates have versions, and a version must be activated before users or automations can run it.

questions.prompt: Which permission set lets a user create and edit prompt templates, as opposed to only running them?

options.text: Prompt Template Manager
Modify All Data
Data Cloud User
Prompt Template User permission set

questions.explanation: Prompt Template Manager allows creating and managing templates; Prompt Template User allows running them.

questions.prompt: Which practice makes a prompt template's output more reliable?

options.text: No grounding, so the model relies on its general knowledge
As few words as possible, so the model is free to decide the details itself
Clear instructions: the role, the task, the format and what to avoid
Several unrelated tasks in one prompt to save calls

questions.explanation: Specific instructions, a stated output format and grounded data reduce vague or invented answers.

questions.prompt: Which is a feature of the Einstein Trust Layer?

options.text: Training the LLM on the org's records each night to improve its answers
Skipping user permissions when the model reads data
Storing customer data with the model provider for reuse
Masking sensitive data before the prompt is sent to the model

questions.explanation: The Trust Layer includes secure data retrieval, data masking, toxicity detection, an audit trail and zero data retention with model providers.

questions.prompt: Why are long documents split into chunks before indexing?

options.text: To translate the documents into the user's language
So retrieval can return the relevant passages, not whole documents
Because Salesforce can't store files longer than a few pages in one record
Because Salesforce can't store files above a few pages

questions.explanation: Chunking breaks text into passages that are embedded and indexed, so retrieval can find and return the most relevant parts.

questions.prompt: What does a search index do in Data 360 retrieval?

options.text: Creates a prompt template for each document it stores
Removes duplicate records before an agent reads them, so answers stay consistent
Runs Apex triggers when new documents are uploaded
Stores chunk embeddings so related text can be found by meaning

questions.explanation: A search index holds the vectors for chunks, enabling semantic (vector) or hybrid search.

questions.prompt: What is a retriever's role when grounding a prompt or agent?

options.text: It sends the finished prompt to the LLM and returns the reply
It masks personal data in the prompt before sending
It activates the latest version of a prompt template
It queries a search index and returns the most relevant chunks

questions.explanation: Retrievers run a search against an index, optionally with filters, and return results that are inserted into the prompt as grounding.

questions.prompt: An admin wants an agent to answer from a set of uploaded PDFs with minimal setup. What should they use?

options.text: An Agentforce Data Library
Pasting the PDFs' contents into the agent's instructions
A report of uploaded files that the agent can read
A custom object that stores the text of each PDF so the agent can query it

questions.explanation: Agentforce Data Libraries handle ingestion, chunking, indexing and retriever setup for files or Knowledge, and connect to the agent.

questions.prompt: Which question is best answered by retrieval over unstructured content, rather than by a record query?

options.text: 'What does our returns policy say about opened items?'
'How many open cases does this account have right now?'
'Who owns this opportunity?'
'What is the status of order 1234?'

questions.explanation: Policy text lives in documents and needs semantic retrieval. Counts, statuses and owners are precise record queries.

questions.prompt: An agent must answer only from articles for the customer's product line. What helps?

options.text: Adding 'only use relevant articles' to the topic instructions
Filters on the retriever, using a field such as product line
Deleting the articles for other product lines
A separate org for each product line's content

questions.explanation: Retriever filters restrict results to matching content, which is more reliable than instructions alone.

questions.prompt: Agents give outdated answers after policy documents were updated. What should be checked?

options.text: The org's default time zone
The model's temperature setting, which may be too low
That the new content was ingested and the index refreshed
Only the model's temperature setting

questions.explanation: Retrieval answers only as well as its indexed content. Confirm the new files were ingested and the index is up to date.

questions.prompt: How does an agent decide which topic handles a user's request?

options.text: It matches the request to each topic's description and scope
The most recently created topic is always tried first
The user picks a topic from a menu before chatting
Topics are tried in alphabetical order until one of them matches the request

questions.explanation: The reasoning engine uses topic descriptions (classification) to pick the topic, then plans which of that topic's actions to run.

questions.prompt: Where should rules like 'always confirm the order number before cancelling' go?

options.text: In the page layout of the Order object
In a report that the agent reads
In the agent's name and welcome message
In the topic's instructions

questions.explanation: Topic instructions guide how the agent behaves within that topic, including which steps to take and in what order.

questions.prompt: Which can be used as a custom agent action?

options.text: A validation rule or a duplicate rule
A dashboard, a report or a list view that the agent can open
A flow, an invocable Apex method or a prompt template
A page layout or a compact layout

questions.explanation: Agent actions can call autolaunched flows, invocable Apex, prompt templates and external services.

questions.prompt: An agent keeps choosing the wrong action. What should be improved first?

options.text: The action's description and input and output descriptions
The total number of topics in the agent
The colour and branding of the chat window the customer sees
The org's default language setting

questions.explanation: The reasoning engine relies on action and input descriptions to decide when and how to call an action. Vague descriptions cause wrong choices.

questions.prompt: A refund action must never run until the customer's identity is verified. What is the most reliable control?

options.text: A longer, more detailed description on the refund topic
An instruction in the topic telling the agent to be very careful with refunds
A verification variable plus a filter on the refund action
A lower temperature on the model the agent uses

questions.explanation: Variables and filters enforce conditions deterministically. Instructions alone can be ignored by the model.

questions.prompt: Internal sales reps want an assistant inside Lightning Experience that acts on records they can access. Which agent type fits?

options.text: An agent for guest users of an Experience Cloud site
A service agent deployed on the public website
An email auto-response rule for the sales team
An employee agent

questions.explanation: Employee agents work for internal users and run with that user's permissions. Service agents serve customers on external channels.

questions.prompt: Under which user context do a service agent's actions run?

options.text: The system administrator who activated the agent, so every action works
The customer's own Salesforce user record
A dedicated agent user with limited permissions
Whichever human agent is online at the time

questions.explanation: Service agents run as a dedicated agent user. Give it only the permissions its actions need.

questions.prompt: An employee agent can't update an opportunity for one rep but can for another. What is the most likely reason?

options.text: The agent is broken for that rep and must be deactivated and activated again
It runs as the signed-in user, who lacks access to that record
The opportunity has too many products for the agent
Employee agents can only read data, never update it

questions.explanation: Employee agents respect the user's sharing and permissions, so results differ by user.

questions.prompt: A service agent should talk to customers on the company website. Which channel is used?

options.text: A Lightning record page on Contact
Web-to-Lead with an assignment rule
Messaging for In-App and Web (Enhanced Chat)
Email-to-Case with an auto-response rule

questions.explanation: Service agents are deployed to customers through Messaging for In-App and Web, and can also be connected to other channels such as Experience Cloud.

questions.prompt: A company's mobile app, built outside Salesforce, needs to hold conversations with an existing agent. What fits?

options.text: The Data Import Wizard
Agent API
Web-to-Case with a hidden form
A Lightning record page embedded in the app

questions.explanation: The Agent API lets external applications start sessions and exchange messages with an agent.

questions.prompt: When should an admin build a custom topic rather than rely on a standard one?

options.text: When the job is business-specific, like warranty checks
Never, because custom topics aren't supported for agents
Always, because standard topics can't be used in production orgs
Only when building an employee agent for internal users

questions.explanation: Standard topics cover common jobs; custom topics are for business-specific tasks with their own instructions and actions.

questions.prompt: An agent sometimes invents order details. What reduces this?

options.text: Add more topics so it has more ways to answer
Ground answers in actions that fetch real data, and allow 'I don't know'
Ask customers to double-check the details it gives
Remove all actions so it answers from its general knowledge only

questions.explanation: Grounding in real data plus clear instructions for unknowns reduces invented answers.

questions.prompt: How can an admin check that an agent picks the right topic and action across 200 sample questions?

options.text: Chat with the agent 200 times by hand and note the results in a spreadsheet
A batch test in Testing Center with expected results
Deploy to production and read through the conversation logs
Run a report on cases created by the agent

questions.explanation: Testing Center runs test cases in bulk and compares the agent's topic, actions and response with expected values.

questions.prompt: Where can test cases for Testing Center come from?

options.text: Only from real production conversations exported each week
An uploaded CSV, or AI-generated test cases
Only from published Knowledge articles
Only typed in one at a time by an admin

questions.explanation: Test cases can be uploaded or generated, then refined. Testing in a sandbox avoids affecting customers.

questions.prompt: Where should agents be built and tested before customers use them?

options.text: In a sandbox, then deployed to production
On the customer website with a 'beta' label
In a Developer Edition org unrelated to the company
Directly in production, since agents can be deactivated

questions.explanation: Build and test in a sandbox with realistic data, then deploy the metadata to production through change sets, DevOps Center or the CLI.

questions.prompt: After deploying an agent to production, an action fails. What should have been checked?

options.text: That every flow, Apex class, template and permission it uses was deployed
That the org-wide defaults were set to Public
That the agent's name was unique across the org and every sandbox
That the sandbox was deleted after the deployment

questions.explanation: Agents depend on other metadata and settings. Missing or inactive dependencies break actions after deployment.

questions.prompt: A prompt template was deployed to production, but the field generation button doesn't appear. What is the likely cause?

options.text: The LLM isn't available in production orgs
Users need a Data Loader licence to run templates
Prompt templates can't be deployed between orgs and must be rebuilt
The template isn't activated, or the page isn't set up

questions.explanation: After deployment, check activation and the record page configuration that exposes the template.

questions.prompt: Compliance wants to review what was sent to the model and what came back. What supports this?

options.text: Field history tracking on Case
Debug logs for the agent user
The Trust Layer's audit trail, stored in Data 360
The org's login history and setup audit trail

questions.explanation: The Trust Layer records prompts, responses and safety scores in an audit trail for review.

questions.prompt: How does the Trust Layer help with harmful outputs?

options.text: It retrains the model each night on flagged responses
It hides flagged responses from administrators
It blocks every response that contains a person's name
It scores responses for toxicity so they can be monitored

questions.explanation: Toxicity detection scores generated content, which is logged for monitoring and review.

questions.prompt: After launch, the team wants to know which requests the agent fails to handle. What should they review?

options.text: The page layout assigned to the agent user
Agent analytics on escalations and unhandled requests
The number of users with Agentforce licences each month
The sandbox refresh history for the org

questions.explanation: Agent analytics and conversation review show where the agent escalates or fails, which drives new topics or better instructions.

questions.prompt: Security wants to restrict which LLMs can be used in the org. Where is this managed?

options.text: In the model settings, where available models are managed
In the Chatter settings for the org
In the case assignment rules for the service team
In each user's profile, under the personal settings for AI

questions.explanation: Admins manage which models are available, including standard and bring-your-own models, so templates and agents only use approved ones.

questions.prompt: One agent has grown to 30 topics and keeps choosing the wrong one. What should be considered?

options.text: Merge all 30 topics into one broad topic
Adding more topics to the same agent so it has more options to choose from
Remove all topic instructions so it decides freely
Splitting it into specialised agents with routing between them

questions.explanation: Too many overlapping topics confuse classification. Specialised agents with clear scopes scale and are easier to control.

questions.prompt: What is the Model Context Protocol (MCP) used for?

options.text: A standard way for agents to reach external tools and data
A data masking algorithm in the Trust Layer
A report type for agent conversations
A Salesforce record sharing model used to control what agents can see

questions.explanation: MCP is an open protocol that lets AI applications discover and call tools and data sources through a common interface.

questions.prompt: What does the Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol address?

options.text: Encrypting agent conversation data at rest in Data 360
Synchronising quotes with opportunities
Routing cases to agents by skill
Communication and task hand-offs between agents

questions.explanation: A2A is an open standard for agents to discover each other's capabilities and exchange tasks across platforms.
